get.description: Returns the public JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) used to verify JWTs issued by this service.
Returns the OpenID Connect discovery document for this service.

delete.description:
Deletes (revokes) an access key by name.
The authenticated user must be able to delete access keys in this workspace.

Once deleted, the access key can no longer be used for authentication.

patch.description:
Updates the metadata of an existing access key without rotating its secret.
The authenticated user must have the `access_key:update` permission in the
workspace.

Only `keyName` and `tokenExpiry` can be changed. The access key secret
continues to authenticate after the update.

Access-key principals are forbidden from calling this endpoint —
credential lifecycle operations must come from a human-authenticated
session, so a leaked access key cannot silently extend its own TTL or
rename itself. The check uses [`PrincipalKind::AccessKey`] (not
`is_cts_minted_token`) because dashboard humans also hold CTS-minted
tokens and must remain allowed.

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters or duplicate name

get.description:
Retrieves all access keys for the authenticated user in the specified workspace.
The user must have list access key permissions.

Returns an array of access keys with metadata including creation date and last usage.

post.description:
Creates a new access key for the workspace.
The authenticated user must have admin privileges in the workspace.

The returned access key can only be retrieved once at creation time.
Store it securely as it cannot be recovered later.

Access keys can be assigned different roles (Admin, Member, Control) to control permissions.

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters or duplicate name

post.description:
Exchange a credential for a CipherStash access token.

## Credential Types

This endpoint accepts two types of credentials:

### OIDC Token
Exchange an OIDC JWT from a configured provider for a CipherStash token.
Requires:
- `oidcToken`: A valid JWT from an OIDC provider configured for the workspace
- `workspaceId`: The workspace to authorize against

### Access Key
Exchange a CipherStash access key for a token.
Requires:
- `accessKey`: A valid CipherStash access key (format: `CSAKT...`)

## Response

Returns a signed JWT (`accessToken`) and an `expiry` timestamp.

get.description:
Lists all memberships for the workspace.

## Authentication

Valid authentication credential must be provided using the `Authorization` header.

* **Access Key** - Requires an access key with the `admin` role.
* **CipherStash ServiceToken** - Requires a ServiceToken (CTS-minted JWT) for a user who is an admin of the workspace.

*NOTE: CipherStash ServiceTokens for human callers are only issued via the CipherStash Dashboard's OIDC exchange flow.*

put.description:
Import a workspace for cross-region migration. Uses replace semantics: if the workspace
already exists, all associated data (access keys, memberships, OIDC providers) is deleted
and recreated from the import payload.

Requires service principal authentication with admin role. The caller's organization must
match the import organization ID.

AccessKeyUpdates.description:
Fields that can be changed on an access key.

Omitted or `null` fields are left unchanged. At least one field must be
present.

`role` is intentionally **not** included — changing an access key's role
post-creation is a privilege-management operation that must go through
delete + recreate, so role changes are always paired with secret rotation.
`deny_unknown_fields` is set so a client trying to send `role` (or any
other unknown field) gets a 400 instead of having the field silently
dropped, which would mask client/server protocol drift or active probing.

OidcVendor.description:
OIDC vendors that we support.

The major difference between `CipherStash` and `Auth0`|`Okta`|`Clerk` is in how we determine workspace membership.
To validate `CipherStash` issued JWTs, we must check the `sub` claim against our membership table.  This is because
the issuer is shared among all workspaces.  In contrast, `Auth0` and all other OIDC vendors are associated with
specific workspaces.

## Issuers associated with multiple workspaces

Note that it is valid for a 3rd party issuer to be associated with more than one workspace.  In this case, users
within the issuer's domain can be members of multiple workspaces.

Constrast this to the `CipherStash` issuer which does not assume that a user is a member of a workspace, simply
because they have a valid JWT.  The membership is determined by the `sub` claim and the workspace ID (by checking
`memberships`).

RawAccessKey.description:
A raw access key that has not yet been verified.
The wrapper ensures safe handling of the key.
This is useful for deserialization from JSON or other formats.

The inner string is zeroized on drop so a full access-key credential does
not linger in freed memory once the `RawAccessKey` goes out of scope.

Equality is `TimingSafeEq` (constant-time), not a plain `derive(PartialEq)`:
this type holds a full credential, so `==` must not leak length/prefix via
timing. Same choice as [`SecretToken`].

Role.description: Defines a role in the system.

updates.description: The fields to update. At least one must be present.
